subject: CardioCloud latency spike / geo-handoff investigation
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@cardiocloud.io>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Ops Team <ops@cardiocloud.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: p95/p99 jump in hosted API since 08:45 PDT

Hi Marcus,

We're seeing a sustained p95 increase from ~120ms to 640ms and p99 spikes up to 1.8s across our production traffic to the Hosted API since ~08:45 PDT. Error rate is still low but throughput has dropped ~12% as clients time out and retry. This is happening for endpoints served from us-west-2 and appears to affect only traffic originating from our EU region clients as well as some east-coast US requests.

Attached is a short perf graph and a set of request ids (example: req_19a7b). Our SREs are seeing RTT increases and a higher hop count on traces that suggest an extra cross-region hop. Can you confirm whether there were any recent routing or peering changes? This is customer-affecting and we need an ETA and mitigation plan.

We are happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Ayesha Khan
Head of Engineering, CardioCloud

Attachments: perf-graphs-2028-04-11.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95/p99 jump in hosted API since 08:45 PDT

Thanks Ayesha — and thanks for the data. Grace/Jonas/Evelyn: can you triage routing and peering immediately? Ask:
- Confirm whether any recent route table changes, peering config edits, or deploys to the edge control plane around 08:30–09:00 PDT.
- Collect traceroutes for sample req ids and share full hop logs (include timestamps)
- If this looks like a cross-region handoff, identify which routing policy caused the extra hop and whether it was a policy rollout or an automated failover.

I copied Vivek and Neha since this is high-touch for CardioCloud and will likely need an executive note and a credit proposal. I'll coordinate comms to CardioCloud once we have a short mitigation plan.

Marcus
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95/p99 jump in hosted API since 08:45 PDT

Marcus — quick update from the infra side.

What we found (initial):
- An automated rollout of a new routing policy (try-by-region v2) completed a staged activation at ~08:33 PDT. The policy contains a fallback mapping that mistakenly treats eu-west-3 as compatible with us-west-2 for a subset of session tokens.
- Traceroutes for provided request ids show an extra inter-region hop: us-west-2 -> eu-west-3 -> us-west-2 in some flows, adding ~420–520ms RTT in aggregate. Hop logs attached.
- No kernel or model changes were deployed at the time.

Immediate mitigation steps we took at 09:58 PDT:
- Rolled back try-by-region v2 to v1 for the affected pool (partial rollback completed at 10:02 PDT).
- Toggled an aggressive route pinning for CardioCloud tenant to ensure direct us-west-2 paths while we root cause the mapping error.

Next steps:
1) Jonas will push a full mapping sanity check to the control plane to remove stale region aliases (Jira INF-4527).
2) Evelyn will run a short canary to validate traffic is no longer crossing regions.
3) We'll produce a short RCA and a corrective rollout plan by EOD.

Attaching trace-hoplog.txt with annotated hops.

Grace
Principal Infra PM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: trace-hoplog.txt
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@cardiocloud.io>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Ops Team <ops@cardiocloud.io>, Purchasing <purchasing@cardiocloud.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: p95/p99 jump in hosted API since 08:45 PDT

Marcus / Grace — thank you for the rapid rollback and the pinning. We're already seeing p95 drop back to ~150–200ms for most requests. There are still occasional p99 spikes ~1.1–1.4s for a small fraction of requests that look like they hit a bad route. We've attached a screenshot from our dashboard showing the before/after.

Can you confirm an ETA for the full mapping sanity check and whether you will provide any goodwill credit for the disruption? Our procurement team is cc'd — they asked for a formal incident summary and a one-off credit proposal to cover excess retries and support time.

We are available for a 30-minute sync if helpful.

—Ayesha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@cardiocloud.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary: CardioCloud RTT surge due to mis-mapped region aliases — next steps

Team / Vivek / Neha — quick exec note to summarize status and proposed customer resolution. Please treat as draft for external incident summary.

What happened:
- At ~08:33 PDT a staged rollout of "try-by-region v2" introduced an erroneous alias mapping (eu-west-3 -> us-west-2) for a subset of session tokens used by CardioCloud. This produced an extra inter-region hop in some flows, increasing RTT and driving p95/p99 regressions.

Impact:
- CardioCloud production p95 rose from ~120ms to 640ms; p99 spikes up to 1.8s briefly. Throughput reduction ~12% due to client timeouts and retries. Affects primarily CardioCloud and a small set of other EU-origin flows.

Immediate actions taken:
- Partial rollback of try-by-region v2 completed at 10:02 PDT.
- Tenant route pinning applied at 10:05 PDT to restore direct paths.
- Ongoing mapping sanity check (INF-4527) to remove stale aliases.

Current status (15:00 PDT):
- Majority of requests restored to expected p95 (120–220ms). Intermittent p99 spikes remain for <0.5% of traffic.

Proposed customer remediation:
- Provide a one-time credit equivalent to two days of excess token throughput (suggested amount: discretionary, finance to finalize).
- Deliver a formal RCA and corrective rollout checklist by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a post-incident sync with CardioCloud SREs to walk through fix and long-term guardrails.

Action items:
- Jonas: complete INF-4527 and post PR for mapping fix by 17:30 PDT (in progress).
- Evelyn: finish canary validation and attest no cross-region hops by 16:30 PDT.
- Grace: prepare the incident timeline and draft RCA.
- Neha/Vivek: advise on credit amount and comms tone for CardioCloud.

I will send the external incident summary to CardioCloud after Neha/Vivek sign-off.

Marcus
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fix-plan-checklist.md
